The Philippines lies along the Pacific Ring of Fire, so it has many volcanoes and earthquakes.
About 20 tropical cyclones enter the Philippine area of responsibility every year.
Typhoon Yolanda (Haiyan) hit the Visayas in November 2013 and was extremely powerful.
Tropical Storm Ondoy (Ketsana) caused severe flooding in Metro Manila in September 2009.
Mount Pinatubo's 1991 eruption was one of the largest of the 20th century.
During an earthquake: Drop, Cover, and Hold On.
A go-bag should hold water, food, a flashlight, a radio, first aid and important documents.
PAGASA issues weather and typhoon warnings in the Philippines.
PHIVOLCS monitors volcanoes and earthquakes in the Philippines.
